author: Sara Palczewski
title: New Orleans Saints yet to name starting QB in close competition - NewsBreak
text: METAIRIE, La. (Louisiana First) — The New Orleans Saints’ quarterback competition is coming down to the wire. The black and gold are the only team in the NFL who have not yet named a starting quarterback. Head coach Kellen Moore said he’s going to let the competition between Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler play out throughout the week and in the third and final preseason game. A big reason why this competition is still ongoing is because of how close it is. Taking a look at the stats from just the first two preseason games, Rattlers completed 71.4% of his passes for 252 yards, a touchdown and one interception. He’s also been sacked three times. Meanwhile, the rookie, Shough, completed 70.6% of his passes for 231 yards, one touchdown, and an interception. He’s also been sacked four times. “It’s close,” Moore said. “We look at every aspect of this quarterback situation, and so it’s really, really close. Numbers, experiences, reps, everything that’s going all the way back to the start of training camp. Everything is very, very close between this group. We’re kind of staying in the middle and obviously, you’d like for it to make a decision, and we’ll get there as we go. I think both these guys are putting in tremendous effort, tremendous work. They’re both doing a ton of good things. So, we’ll see how it goes.” Moore said both Rattler and Shough will play in Saturday’s preseason finale against the Denver Broncos. However, he would not name a starter as of Wednesday’s practice. Moore said he would not keep who the starter is for Week 1 against the Arizona Cardinals a secret once the decision is made. But what happens once the decision is made: does the competition keep going on between Rattler and Shough? “I think we’re going to name a guy and everyone’s gonna rally behind that guy,” Moore said. “And that guy’s the guy and everyone’s there to support him. He’s going to throw an interception at some point and we’re not going to have to look over his back. He’s the guy. Everyone else has a really big time opportunity to continue to develop. Again, this is a developmental opportunity for all these quarterbacks. They’re all young. We’re gonna keep developing and opportunities will present themselves for all these guys and in some aspect down the line as well.” For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to Louisiana First News.
